title: Blueprints, landing zones and the Cloud Adoption Framework

videos.script: A new team gets a new subscription. What is in it? {{empty}} If somebody made it by hand, almost nothing. No budget, no network, no rules. It sits under the tenant root, governed by nobody. {{root}} A landing zone is the opposite. It is a subscription that arrives ready, like a plot with the water and the power already connected. {{plot}} Microsoft's Cloud Adoption Framework describes it in two halves. A platform, built once for everybody. And workload zones, one per application. {{halves}} It also publishes a tree of management groups. That tree is not split by environment. Staging sits beside production, under the same rules, so that a test means something. {{tree}} You will write that tree in Bicep, and meet a loop that has to run one step at a time. {{loop}} Then the tool that used to do all this. Blueprints is being retired, and two features replace it. {{retire}} Template specs keep the versions. Deployment stacks remember what they built, and can stop anyone deleting it. {{end}}
